name: query_service.py
summary: Orchestrates query execution by coordinating data access, AI translation, caching, and user validation.
purpose: Acts as a central orchestrator in the query domain to process and execute data queries, abstracting the complexity of interacting with datasets, AI services, caching layers, and user management behind a unified service interface.
responsibilities: Delegating data persistence to QueryRepository and DatasetRepository
Integrating AI-powered query generation or translation via AIQueryService
Managing result caching and cache invalidation through CacheService
Coordinating user validation, authorization, and context via UserService
Applying Django settings for query configuration and runtime behavior
inputs: Query definitions or natural language requests
Query parameters, filters, and execution options
outputs: Query execution results or result sets
Validation errors, permission denials, or execution exceptions
architecture_notes: Implements the Service Layer and Facade patterns to decouple the query domain from infrastructure concerns. It coordinates multiple repositories and external services (AI, cache, users), suggesting an orchestrator role within a layered Django architecture. The high number of direct dependencies indicates a God Service anti-pattern risk; it likely serves as the primary entry point for query-related business logic.
improvements: Apply the Single Responsibility Principle by decomposing into smaller services (e.g., QueryValidator, QueryExecutor, QueryCacheManager)
Introduce an abstract interface or ABC for QueryService to improve testability and enable mocking
Use dependency injection rather than direct concrete class imports to reduce coupling and increase modularity
Add explicit transaction boundaries if multiple repositories are consulted in a single workflow
Consider implementing a CQRS pattern if read/query logic diverges significantly from command/write logic
